topStories.headline: D8 Race Reshuffled: SF Dems Endorse McCoy, New Poll Shows Two-Candidate Fight
topStories.dek: After dumping Manny Yekutiel, the city's Democratic Party swung behind Gary McCoy — but a new poll puts Darshini Patel within striking distance with 18 days to go.
topStories.body:
The District 8 supervisor race, which covers the Castro, Noe Valley, Glen Park and surrounding neighborhoods, was jolted into a new shape this week after the San Francisco Democratic Party formally rescinded its endorsement of Emanuel "Manny" Yekutiel and threw its weight behind Gary McCoy. At a tense special meeting on October 11, the Democratic County Central Committee voted 29-0 to pull Yekutiel's endorsement and then 20-8 to back McCoy, according to the Bay Area Reporter. Former Supervisor Gordon Mar resigned from the DCCC amid the tumult.

McCoy, a former political director for Congressmember Nancy Pelosi who is in recovery from addiction, has assembled an unusually wide coalition since Yekutiel dropped out on October 1 following a second sexual-assault allegation. Supervisor Rafael Mandelman — who initially stood by Yekutiel on the morning the new allegations broke before pulling his support that same afternoon — has now endorsed McCoy, as have a supermajority of sitting Board of Supervisors members, State Sen. Scott Wiener, the Alice B. Toklas and Harvey Milk LGBTQ Democratic clubs, and the SF Labor Council. A moderate-aligned political group added its endorsement on October 14, the SF Standard reported.

But a GrowSF poll of 421 likely District 8 voters, conducted October 5–9 and published October 12, suggests the race remains unsettled. McCoy and Darshini Patel — a former DoorDash executive and Kamala Harris campaign staffer who lives in Noe Valley — were within the poll's 5-percent margin of error. Brad Chapin, Yekutiel's original accuser, subsequently announced he is endorsing Patel. The third active candidate is patent attorney and drag performer Michael Nguyen, who trails in the survey.

Yekutiel's name remains on the November 3 ranked-choice ballot despite his withdrawal. Voter guides from both the SF Chronicle and GrowSF warn that votes cast for Yekutiel will not advance toward the outcome. With three viable candidates remaining, election groups are urging District 8 voters — in the Castro, Noe Valley, Glen Park, Diamond Heights, and Duboce Triangle — to rank all three active candidates to keep their ballots live through each round of counting.

topStories.headline: Glen Park Is Getting a New Mosaic Mural — and You Can Weigh In This Wednesday
topStories.dek: Renowned Bay Area artist Dana Albany will share her initial design for a courtyard mural next to Pono Boutique at a public comment session at the Glen Park branch library.
topStories.body:
Glen Park Beautiful is bringing artist Dana Albany to the neighborhood for a new mosaic mural project, and the public is invited to see the first draft and comment before work begins. The session is set for Wednesday, October 21, from 6:30 to 7:30 p.m. at the Glen Park Branch Library, 2825 Diamond Street.

According to a Glen Park Association post published October 14 by project leader Renee A. Berger, the mural will be installed at the rear of the courtyard next to Pono Boutique. Albany is a San Francisco Bay Area artist known for large-scale mosaic installations; her portfolio includes public works commissioned by the City of San Francisco, the California Academy of Sciences, and community projects in the Portola District.

The planned piece would be the latest in a string of neighborhood beautification efforts Glen Park has undertaken in recent years, including the Burnside Mural+, tiled stairways along the Glen Park Greenway, and mosaic work on the Bosworth Pedestrian Bridge — the latter completed in September 2026 and described by the Glen Park Association as now featuring "a lovely sky blue complemented by gorgeous mosaics on its pillars inspired by Indigenous patterns." Glen Park Beautiful is asking attendees to register in advance; a link is available on the Glen Park Association website at glenparkassociation.org.

topStories.headline: Two Transit Measures on Your November 3 Ballot — What Muni Riders Here Need to Know
topStories.dek: Prop H and the regional Connect Bay Area measure together could close Muni's deficit; if both fail, the agency warns of sweeping route cuts, halved frequency, and the end of late-night service.
topStories.body:
San Francisco voters will decide the fate of two interlocking transit funding measures on November 3: Proposition H, a local parcel tax, and Proposition RTM, the Connect Bay Area regional sales tax. Transit advocates say both must pass to keep Muni running at current levels.

Prop H would establish a 15-year parcel tax on most San Francisco properties, running from July 2027 through June 2042. The tax is based on building square footage rather than assessed value. The San Francisco Chamber of Commerce estimates it would raise about $177 million annually; SPUR projects roughly $160 million. Under the current structure, single-family homeowners would pay $129 per year, multifamily property owners $249, and non-residential property owners $799, with additional amounts for large-footprint buildings. The Chamber has endorsed Prop H.

Prop RTM — the Connect Bay Area initiative, authorized by SB 63 authored by State Sen. Scott Wiener — would add a 1-percent sales tax in San Francisco (and 0.5 percent in four neighboring Bay Area counties) for 14 years. GrowSF estimates that would raise $155 million annually for Muni alone, on top of funding for BART, Caltrain, and other regional agencies. The measure needs a simple majority across the five-county district rather than county by county. SPUR warns that without both measures passing, Muni may be forced to cut up to 20 routes entirely, reduce buses and trains by half, end service by 9 p.m., and eliminate historic cable car lines — changes that would directly affect the J-Church, 24-Divisadero, 33-Ashbury/18th, and other lines that serve these neighborhoods daily.

A community information session on both measures was held October 15 at Most Holy Redeemer Church in the Castro, co-hosted by the Glen Park Association and more than a dozen neighborhood groups including the Eureka Valley Neighborhood Association, the Duboce Triangle Neighborhood Association, and the Cole Valley Improvement Association.

moreNews.headline: Yekutiel Is Still on the D8 Ballot — Ranked-Choice Voters Should Plan Accordingly
moreNews.body: Despite withdrawing from the District 8 supervisor race on October 1, Manny Yekutiel's name will appear on the November 3 ranked-choice ballot, confirmed by both the SF Chronicle voter guide and GrowSF's voter analysis published this week. Votes cast for Yekutiel as a first, second, or third choice will not count toward the final outcome. With three active candidates — Gary McCoy, Darshini Patel, and Michael Nguyen — voter groups are encouraging District 8 residents to rank all three to ensure their ballot remains live through each round of counting.
